properties.title: A Bayesian Reasoning Framework for Robotic Systems in Autonomous Casualty Triage

properties.name: Expert CPT BN with ROS2 multi-robot perception

raw_results.scenario: DTC Round1 Systems Competition, two runs, staged casualties
raw_results.training_test_split: No learned CPT training; field evaluation after expert elicitation; independent held-out split not stated
raw_results.scope_unresolved_reason: Mixed volunteer/manikin breakdown absent; TableIII and Figure3 limb counts disagree; abstract run percentages misalign with score ratios

runtime_claim.scope: BN update only; hardware-specific timing protocol unspecified

properties.design: DTC Round1 staged two-mission robot+BN comparison
properties.environment: healthy volunteers portraying casualties and mannequins
properties.independence: Reported tables overlap; do not double-count as independent clinical evidence

properties.basis: Same named Team Chiron/DTC Round1,11+9 staged casualties; all per-casualty score rows and nine vital-assignment rows agree exactly. Titles and author lists differ.
properties.independence_assessment: Treat as dependent reporting, not two independent20case validations; underlying participant/session identity not independently confirmed.

scope.population: 20 staged casualties: healthy volunteers and TOMManikin; exact breakdown unreported
scope.time_horizon: Current condition inference at scan completion/fixed cadence

assertions.rationale: Fixed-cadence reinference imputes current variables using a static BN; no model maps carried health state to future time. Timestamped sensors and evidence updates do not establish a temporal transition.

scope.population: 20 staged casualties: healthy volunteers and TOMManikin; exact breakdown unreported
scope.time_horizon: Current condition inference at scan completion/fixed cadence

assertions.rationale: Expert CPT graph infers concurrent condition variables; no latent transition model.

scope.population: 20 staged casualties: healthy volunteers and TOMManikin; exact breakdown unreported
scope.time_horizon: Current condition inference at scan completion/fixed cadence

assertions.rationale: BN posterior represents uncertainty over named current physiological variables conditioned on observed categorical inputs.

scope.population: 20 staged casualties: healthy volunteers and TOMManikin; exact breakdown unreported
scope.time_horizon: Current condition inference at scan completion/fixed cadence

assertions.rationale: New time-stamped categorical inputs trigger inference, but persistent filtering/correction and evidence-age/replacement policy are not described.
criteria_missing: Persistent prior propagation/correction and stale evidence policy

scope.population: 20 staged casualties: healthy volunteers and TOMManikin; exact breakdown unreported
scope.time_horizon: Current condition inference at scan completion/fixed cadence

assertions.rationale: Named injury/vital-sign variables and heuristic CPT elicitation are documented; users’ inspection of state/posterior interface is future work.

scope.time_horizon: Current condition inference at scan completion/fixed cadence

assertions.rationale: Cross-platform matching aggregates observations by casualty, but ID-switch/duplicate audit is absent.

scope.time_horizon: Current condition inference at scan completion/fixed cadence

assertions.rationale: Predictions are time-stamped but native acquisition clock conventions/units and synchronization are unspecified.
criteria_missing: Native measurement clock and synchronization semantics

scope.time_horizon: Current condition inference at scan completion/fixed cadence

assertions.rationale: Unobserved categorical variables are marginalized, but full availability-mask representation and train/runtime semantics are not specified.

legacy_cells.B: A Bayesian Reasoning Framework for Robotic Systems in Autonomous Casualty Triage
legacy_cells.C: Szymon Rusiecki; Cecilia Morales; Pia Störy; Kimberly Elenberg; Leonard Weiss; Artur Dubrawski
legacy_cells.I: 060_2026_A Bayesian Reasoning Framework for Robotic Systems in Autonomous Casualty Triage.pdf
legacy_cells.O: Mass-casualty trauma and life-threatening injuries, including severe hemorrhage, respiratory distress, head/torso/extremity trauma, and alertness
legacy_cells.S: Can fusing robot perception outputs with a Bayesian Network improve casualty triage assessments in mass-casualty scenarios?
legacy_cells.T: 20 casualties in two scenarios, comprising human volunteers and TOMManikin high-fidelity manikins with varied injuries and postures
legacy_cells.V: Assign casualty triage assessments from remotely sensed physiological signs and visible injuries
legacy_cells.AI: Time-stamped predictions from independent perception estimators (e.g., severe hemorrhage and ocular alertness), derived from onboard visual and audio sensing
legacy_cells.AM: Bayesian Network inference fuses heterogeneous estimator predictions as uncertain evidence into a posterior over the casualty’s physiological state
legacy_cells.AN: Marginalizes over unobserved variables and imputes missing information from available evidence
legacy_cells.AT: Bayesian inference updates the casualty posterior as new time-stamped estimator predictions become available; unobserved variables are marginalized
legacy_cells.BN: Expert-defined graph and heuristic conditional probability tables encode clinical dependencies; examples include amputation associated with severe hemorrhage
legacy_cells.BS: Posterior over the casualty’s physiological state and a resulting triage profile
legacy_cells.BT: Physiological-sign/injury estimates and triage assessment returned to the scoring module
legacy_cells.DN: DARPA Triage Challenge (DTC) Round 1 Systems Competition
legacy_cells.DQ: 20 casualty cases across two scenarios (Run A and Run B)
legacy_cells.EC: Triage/assignment performance: overall Performance 14% (Robot) vs 53% (Robot + BN); Reliability 0.31 vs 0.95; Accuracy 46% vs 56%. Run A score 25 vs 61 and Run B score 16 vs 45.
legacy_cells.EG: Inference time less than 1 millisecond per update; memory footprint below 100 megabytes
legacy_cells.EI: Non-WM baseline: direct perception-pipeline outputs (Robot). Robot + BN outperformed Robot: scores 25 vs 61 in Run A and 16 vs 45 in Run B; overall Performance 14% vs 53%. Random-classifier baseline also shown in Figure 3.
legacy_cells.EL: A hardware-level failure before deployment prevented consistent data acquisition for the third run; the system could not locate one casualty in Run B.
legacy_cells.ER: Experiments were conducted in accordance with the Institutional Review Board; approval body or number not stated
legacy_cells.FB: Explicit categorical Bayesian graph of casualty physiological signs and injuries; no learned latent temporal state
legacy_cells.FL: Independent perception-estimator nodes produce time-stamped findings → expert-elicited Bayesian Network over casualty signs/injuries → posterior triage assessment → scoring module; no temporal dynamics model or planner is evaluated.
legacy_cells.FM: Authors list a robotic triage architecture centered on an expert-elicited Bayesian Network, a reasoning framework for noisy/incomplete sensory data, and field validation against independent perception outputs.
legacy_cells.FN: In two scenarios involving 20 casualty cases, Robot + BN achieved scores of 61 vs 25 (Run A) and 45 vs 16 (Run B); overall Performance was 53% vs 14%, Reliability 0.95 vs 0.31, and Accuracy 56% vs 46%.
legacy_cells.FO: Third run excluded after a hardware-level failure prevented consistent data acquisition; one casualty was not located in Run B. Authors note the absence of relevant public standardized datasets, the need for further robustness testing, and possible cascading errors from perception modules.
legacy_cells.FP: Authors propose human-robot teaming and oversight, additional robustness testing, and collecting relevant field data; they also call for comparison with deterministic, probabilistic, rule-based, and hybrid approaches.
legacy_cells.FQ: Authors identify a gap in integrating isolated perception-model outputs into a robust system that assesses each casualty as a whole under noisy and incomplete sensing.
legacy_cells.FR: The study demonstrates improved triage assessment by Bayesian evidence fusion, not a learned or hybrid temporal transition model: no future-state rollouts, action-conditioned alternatives, identified treatment effects, or planning results are reported. Field scenarios used volunteers/manikins and do not establish patient benefit or clinical deployment readiness.
legacy_cells.FT: A reusable design lesson is to keep perception estimators modular and fuse their uncertain categorical outputs in an explicit expert graph that can marginalize missing evidence.
legacy_cells.FX: PDF pp. 1–7: title/byline and abstract; introduction and related work; all Methods subsections (environment, architecture/integration, robotic platform, expert knowledge elicitation); Tables I–III and Figures 1–3 captions/available extracted text; Results including real-time performance; Discussion; Conclusion/future work; acknowledgments and references. Form-feed page breaks inspected throughout. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: The complete seven-page extracted text was read. Tables II–III contain some column/row alignment artifacts in text extraction; the results above use the accompanying prose and clearly extracted reported values. The paper demonstrates expert-rule Bayesian evidence fusion for staged robotic triage, not learned/hybrid temporal state dynamics or action-conditioned planning. A:I were left untouched; source folder and filename metadata were not treated as scientific evidence. Evidence QA: 10/62 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (16.1%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Schema normalization (source details retained): N normalized to 'Other'; source detail: Emergency / prehospital / triage Codex audit: 57 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 5 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: Model-assisted full-source review, no independent human review.
Field tests simulate casualties using volunteers/manikins, not injured-patient care or therapeutic outcome evaluation.
Expert CPTs are heuristic; detector confidence incorporation/calibration/spurious-input rejection and human oversight remain future.
One of three missions excluded due hardware failure; small sample and no independent split limit generalization.
Abstract run percentages and Figure3 limb rates conflict with tables; all preserved separately.
Treat as dependent reporting, not two independent20case validations; underlying participant/session identity not independently confirmed.
